title: Relative spectra of quasi-coherent algebras over algebraic stacks
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal Z$ be an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and let $\mathcal C$ be a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$-algebra [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Schemes, algebraic spaces and $2$-fibre products use [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Define a fibred groupoid $V$ whose objects over a scheme $T$ are pairs $(z,\alpha)$ with $z\in\mathcal Z(T)$ and an $\mathcal O_T$-algebra map $\alpha:z^*\mathcal C\to\mathcal O_T$; its arrows are arrows of $\mathcal Z$ compatible with these algebra maps. Then $V$ is an algebraic stack, and the projection $q:V\to\mathcal Z$ is representable by schemes and affine: for every scheme $u:T\to\mathcal Z$, the $2$-fibre product $V\times_{\mathcal Z}T$ is the scheme $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_T(u^*\mathcal C)$ obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}((u^*\mathcal C)(U))$ over affine opens $U\subseteq T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Formation of $V$, including this identification, commutes with arbitrary base change of algebraic stacks by tensor pullback of $\mathcal C$. The tautological map induces an isomorphism of quasi-coherent algebras $\mathcal C\xrightarrow{\sim}q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal O_V$, where the right adjoint has the meaning and smooth-test interpretation of [lem-sfb-stack-affine-algebra-direct-image]. Consequently $\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ is the ring map induced by the tautological evaluation. The construction is contravariantly functorial in algebra maps. If $\mathcal Z$ is an algebraic space, $V$ is an algebraic space and is its relative spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathcal Z}(\mathcal C)$ in the sense of [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence]. No finiteness, flatness or reducedness hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ is imposed.

proof.text: For an object $z\in\mathcal Z(T)$ write $C_z$ for its ordinary quasi-coherent algebra on $T$. The scheme-test restriction theorem identifies $C_z$ and all its algebra operations with the restriction of $\mathcal C$: its fully faithful tensor-compatible comparison carries the multiplication and unit to the ordinary ones. For an arrow $z'\to z$ over $h:T'\to T$ it gives $h^*C_z\simeq C_{z'}$, with identity and composition compatibility. Pull a pair $(z,\alpha)$ back to $(z',h^*\alpha)$, identifying $h^*\mathcal O_T$ with $\mathcal O_{T'}$. The compatible arrows define a category fibred in groupoids $V$: a cartesian lift in $\mathcal Z$ with this pulled-back algebra map is a lift in $V$, and the unique factorization of arrows in $\mathcal Z$ also preserves these algebra maps. Forgetting $\alpha$ defines $q$.

source.place: Tags 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent), 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), 06WH (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent); fibred-category pullback of the evaluation data

proof.text: Fix $u:T\to\mathcal Z$ and let $A=C_u$. The scheme anti-equivalence gives an affine $p:X=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_T(A)\to T$ with $A\simeq p_*\mathcal O_X$, whose inverse image over an affine open $U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A(U))$. For any $h:W\to T$, scheme relative-Spec base change identifies $X\times_TW$ with $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_W(h^*A)$. A $T$-map $W\to X$ is exactly a section of this base change. Apply the fully faithful anti-equivalence over $W$ to this section: the identity $W\to W$ corresponds to $\mathcal O_W$, so sections correspond bijectively to $\mathcal O_W$-algebra maps $h^*A\to\mathcal O_W$. Both directions are the section maps specified by the anti-equivalence. Under a further pullback they pull back that same algebra map, since the canonical scheme base-change comparison is defined by the structure-sheaf map. Thus the bijection is natural in $W$ and the universal section map is the displayed $A\simeq p_*\mathcal O_X$. This derives the needed universal property rather than assuming that an anti-equivalence restricted to affine objects already states it for an arbitrary $W$.

Over a scheme $W$, an object of $V\times_{\mathcal Z}T$ is $((z,\alpha),h:W\to T,\theta:z\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*u)$. Use $\theta$ and the scheme-test tensor comparison to carry $\alpha$ to $\beta:h^*C_u\to\mathcal O_W$. Conversely $(h,\beta)$ gives the object $((h^*u,\beta),h,1)$. Every original object has a unique arrow to this normalized object compatible with its specified $\theta$; two normalized objects have an arrow over the identity of $W$ exactly when $h$ and $\beta$ agree, and then the arrow is the identity. These operations commute with pullbacks by the composition compatibility in step 1. Step 2 therefore gives an equivalence over $T$ with the discrete fibred groupoid of the scheme $X$. In particular no stabilizers of $\mathcal Z$ survive this fibre product: the isomorphism $\theta$ is part of its data.

source.place: The pair functor in section-spec and Tag 01LX; algebraic.tex Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic), scheme-test hypothesis

proof.text: Step 3 proves representability by schemes, and the scheme projections are affine by step 2. Regard those schemes as algebraic spaces. The representable-source algebraicity theorem applies to the morphism of fibred categories $q$ and the algebraic target $\mathcal Z$, giving that $V$ is an algebraic stack; its statement explicitly requires no prior stack hypothesis on $V$. Only its first assertion is used, so neither local finite presentation of $q$ nor of $\mathcal Z$ is needed. The affine-chart descriptions in step 2 are exactly the requested gluing description.

Let $b:\mathcal Z'\to\mathcal Z$ be any map of algebraic stacks. An object of $V\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal Z'$ is a pair $(z',\alpha)$ after eliminating its specified isomorphism as in step 3; now $\alpha:(z')^*b^*\mathcal C\to\mathcal O_T$. This is precisely the construction for $(\mathcal Z',b^*\mathcal C)$, since scheme-test restriction identifies precomposition with tensor pullback. The two equivalences are inverse on normalized objects and on their arrows. On a scheme $T\to\mathcal Z'$ the resulting scheme identification is the one of step 2 for the same evaluation map. After a further scheme base change it is the canonical scheme relative-Spec comparison, not an independently chosen isomorphism. For an algebra map $\varphi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, send $(z,\alpha:z^*\mathcal D\to\mathcal O_T)$ to $(z,\alpha\circ z^*\varphi)$. Identity and composition hold by substitution, and this operation commutes with the preceding base-change equivalence.

At an object $(z,\alpha)$ of $V$, evaluate a section of $C_z$ by $\alpha$. Compatibility of the arrows of $V$ makes these maps a morphism of algebra sheaves $q^*\mathcal C\to\mathcal O_V$; the scheme-test comparison identifies its source with the stated tensor pullback. Since $q$ is now an affine map of algebraic stacks, the algebra adjunction gives $\eta:\mathcal C\to B:=q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal O_V$. On a smooth scheme test $u:T\to\mathcal Z$, the direct-image theorem identifies $B_u$ with $p_*\mathcal O_X$ for the affine scheme $X$ of step 2. Under this comparison the adjunct of evaluation is the universal algebra map $C_u\to p_*\mathcal O_X$, hence the isomorphism of the scheme anti-equivalence. In particular $\eta_u$ is an isomorphism of ordinary quasi-coherent algebras on every such smooth test.

To pass from smooth tests to the big-site sheaf, choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:U\to\mathcal Z$. For any object $z:T\to\mathcal Z$, the algebraic space $P=T\times_{\mathcal Z}U$ has an etale scheme cover $\{W_i\to P\}$. Base-change and composition of smooth and surjective representable morphisms make $\{W_i\to T\}$ a jointly surjective smooth family. The map $\eta$ restricted to each $W_i$ is the tensor pullback of the isomorphism $\eta_a$ along $W_i\to U$, by scheme-test restriction. The same holds on $W_i\times_TW_j$ by pulling back from $W_i$. Apply smooth-cover section descent on the scheme $T$ to the two quasi-coherent algebras $C_z$ and $B_z$ (viewed on its big fppf site by the slice comparison). Their section rings are the equalizers on this family, and $\eta$ gives isomorphisms of all the displayed rings and the overlap rings. It therefore gives a bijection $\mathcal C(z)=\Gamma(T,C_z)\to B(z)=\Gamma(T,B_z)$. This holds for every $z$, and the inverses commute with restrictions because $\eta$ does. Thus $\eta$ is an isomorphism of algebra sheaves. This argument also covers the empty scheme and uses no quasi-compactness of the atlas or of the relations.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), smooth-cover descent of sections; Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), cartesian scheme restrictions

proof.text: Taking global sections of $\eta$ and then using the natural ring isomorphism $\Gamma(\mathcal Z,q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal O_V)\simeq\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ gives the asserted isomorphism. It is the tautological evaluation map: the adjunct was defined in step 6 by the evaluation at every pair $(z,\alpha)$, and the global-section comparison is the one from this adjunction. Multiplication and algebra maps are preserved by that comparison; its naturality and the substitution formula in step 5 give the claimed functoriality also for global sections.

Finally suppose $\mathcal Z$ is an algebraic space. An automorphism of $(z,\alpha)$ in $V(T)$ projects to an automorphism of $z$, hence is the identity, because the space has discrete fibre groupoids. The algebraic-setoid theorem identifies $V$ with an algebraic space. Its morphism to $\mathcal Z$ is affine by step 3. On an affine etale chart $u:T\to\mathcal Z$, step 2 identifies its structure algebra with $C_u$ by the tautological map. The scheme Zariski/etale quasi-coherent equivalence identifies this with the restriction of the algebra on $\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{et}}$; restriction to affine etale charts and their arrows gives the same section maps. Thus $q_*\mathcal O_V$ on that site is the given algebra. The algebraic-space anti-equivalence identifies this affine space with $\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathcal Z}(\mathcal C)$ and identifies the arrow associated to $\varphi$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_T)$ on every affine etale chart, as in step 5. All previous arguments applied to arbitrary quasi-coherent algebras and arbitrary tensor pullbacks, so no finite generation, flatness, or reducedness restriction has entered.

split_report.summary: Proved the fibred-pair construction by deriving its scheme-test universal property from existing scheme relative-Spec nodes, explicitly normalizing 2-fibre-product objects, and applying representable-source algebraicity. Proved arbitrary base change and contravariant functoriality on objects and arrows. Constructed the tautological algebra map via the affine QCoh adjunction and verified its invertibility on all big-site objects using smooth section descent, without assuming a smooth-only comparison holds on arbitrary tests. Identified the algebraic-space case via trivial stabilizers and the existing space anti-equivalence. No statement change and no new nodes; no source declaration states the entire item.

Step 8: natural global-section isomorphism. Step 9: trivial automorphisms give a space via the setoid lemma, then the Zariski/étale equivalence and the space relative-spec anti-equivalence.
